cells.tense: These days you can move on something while the people around you are still deciding, and neither of those has to give way.
cells.ask: Before you start the next task with someone nearby, say one plain sentence about what you're doing and leave it at that. It shows you how much gets handled instead of said.
cells.core:
You build fast and you stay in touch while you build. When someone's slower, you let them be slower and find the next thing that works for both of you. That's why people around you feel pulled along without being dragged, and they bring you their side of the plan because they know you'll hear it.

What's left for this to feed is trying it out loud. The direction is already yours and it doesn't need defending — so you can take one thing you're about to do today and say a single sentence about it to whoever's nearby, no explaining and no asking. That gives the people close to you a handle on you, and it hands you back the sound of your own direction.
cells.sheetLine: You lead without leaving anyone behind.
cells.verb: moving first and letting people catch up when they can
cells.place: in the part of your life where you're with people

cells.tense: You're already at the end of this in your head, and the people around you haven't even been told there's a change coming.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been pushing toward with someone and say only what you want out of it, no plan attached. You'll find out what it was doing to the two of you.
cells.core:
You can move a shared plan along faster than anyone around you. When you use that well, the people close to you get somewhere they wouldn't have reached alone, and they're glad you pushed — they ask you to push, and they stay in the room while you do it, which is how you know it's welcome.

What bends it is working out every step before anyone gets a say — you're building a version of the future that keeps needing them to hurry. The pressure lands on the people you're trying to move, and being managed stops feeling like being cared for. The effort was for them, and it's costing you them.
cells.sheetLine: You're pushing a plan nobody has agreed to yet.
cells.verb: moving first and letting people catch up when they can
cells.place: in the part of your life where you're with people

cells.tense: There's something you meant to carry to the people near you, and it stayed where it was.
cells.ask: Ask one person you trust for one concrete thing you need this week. It's a sentence with an end, and it tells you what reaching out actually costs here.
cells.core:
You know when something with the people around you needs to change, and you can do it without a scene — you say the thing, and people know where they stand with you. That's the ordinary shape of it, and it's still in you. Conversations with you have edges, and people trust those edges.

What's missing is the asking. You decide how a conversation will go before you've had it, so the ones close to you get your arrangements and not your part in them. You're still at the door, on time, saying nothing. Something in you still wants to say it; the sentence just isn't coming.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the peace and skip the conversation you've already decided will go wrong.
cells.verb: moving first and letting people catch up when they can
cells.place: in the part of your life where you're with people

cells.tense: The push is running on its own by now, and whatever started it is nowhere in the room.
cells.ask: Say one sentence, out loud, about why you're doing today's task, before you start it. It tells you whether anything you're doing still has a reason.
cells.core:
On a normal day with this working, you pick the thing to move because it matters to you, and the people around you can hear that in the way you talk about it. They stay close to the work because you're close to it, and your steady push gives them a floor to stand on.

What's happening instead is that the moving runs on its own. You find the next task in a group the way you'd find the next item on a list, and doing it has quietly become what you offer the people closest to you. The drive is doing the connecting for you, and it holds up less than it looks like it does.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the work moving. You can't say why anymore, and people can feel that.
cells.handle: ...less than it looks like it does.
cells.verb: moving first and letting people catch up when they can
cells.place: in the part of your life where you're with people
